touches.text: A device owns its state: only the device writes under its own ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ tree.

A trouble ticket is a work order. Whoever fixed it reports the fix to the originator (the device or machine that raised it), and the originator marks it fixed. A trouble that comes back is not designed for yet; if recurrent problems appear, we'll explore that.

Its web panel is the operator's to-do list: email, trouble tickets, open questions (the ones only the operator can answer). The list is live: items appear as they arrive and leave as they're answered or resolved.

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.

CC over ssh is told from Akien by the key sshd accepted: CC on each box gets a dedicated ssh key. Until it lands, approve and the operator close refuse any sshd-session caller, Akien's included (Q#115). -amm

claude_code is an admin, elevating on request rather than standing elevated, and CC may talk to other CCs over the inter-CC messaging and use ssh to set up and fix boxes like an IT admin. WHY: Akien uses CC for IT work on his boxes, and two CCs together can fix what one box alone cannot see. -amm

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.
